objective: Catch errors about what RAG and fine-tuning change.

sources.title: Lewis et al. 2020, Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (NeurIPS)

followUp: Name one task where fine-tuning would be a better fit than RAG, and say why.

transfer.scenario: A supplier-quality team wants an assistant that knows each supplier's current corrective-action status. Someone suggests fine-tuning a model on last year's reports. Respond.
rubric: fine-tuning bakes in stale facts|retraining needed
exact status better from database or API

narration.text: Our support team wants an assistant that answers from our internal policy documents.
Prompting alone won't work, because the policies run to thousands of pages and change every month.
So we'll use RAG. RAG retrains the model on your company documents, so it learns our policies.
When a policy changes, we update the index, and the next question can use the new text.
Because answers come from retrieved passages, we can show users which document each answer used.
Fine-tuning would also be the best way to keep the assistant current with each month's policy changes.
If we later want a consistent tone and format in replies, fine-tuning is one option to evaluate.

planted.misconception: RAG retrains the model on your company documents.
planted.whyWrong: RAG retrieves relevant passages at query time and puts them in the prompt. The model's weights do not change; the knowledge lives in a separate index.
acceptableCorrections: RAG retrieves relevant passages at question time and adds them to the prompt; the model isn't retrained.
With RAG the model reads our documents per question; it doesn't learn them into its weights.
planted.exceptions: The original 2020 RAG paper fine-tuned its query encoder and generator on task examples, but the document encoder was kept fixed and the document knowledge stayed in a swappable index. Typical production RAG on a hosted model involves no training.

planted.misconception: Fine-tuning is the way to keep knowledge current.
planted.whyWrong: Fine-tuning changes weights, so each policy change would need a new training run, evaluation and release. Facts learned this way can't be cited or permission-filtered. Updating a RAG index is the usual way to stay current.
acceptableCorrections: To stay current we re-sync the RAG index; fine-tuning would need retraining every month.
Fine-tuning suits style and format; changing facts belong in retrieval.
planted.exceptions: Fine-tuning can complement RAG for tone or format (s7 is correct).
